question:
A 52-year-old carpenter complains of difficult gripping a hammer, which worsens with repeated use. On
physical exam, he is able to passively flex the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint when the
metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint is flexed but not when the MCP joint is extended. What is the most
likely explanation? Answer Choices: (A) Extrinsic tightness (B) Neuropathy of the ulnar nerve (C) Joint
capsule contracture of the PIP joint (D) Intrinsic tightness (E) Lumbrical muscle weakness (F) Trigger
finger phenomenon (G) Flexor tendon rupture (H) Volar plate injury (I) Adhesion of the flexor tendons
(J) Central slip rupture
 A. Lumbrical muscle weakness
B. Central slip rupture
C. Adhesion of the flexor tendons
D. Joint capsule contracture of the PIP joint
E. Flexor tendon rupture
F. Neuropathy of the ulnar nerve
G. Intrinsic tightness
H. Volar plate injury
I. Extrinsic tightness
J. Trigger finger phenomenon
